title: Big Soccer Fight Won't Stop the U-20 Women's World Cup!
summary: Have you ever had a fight with a friend but still went to their party? That's kind of what's happening in soccer right now! There's a big argument between FIFA, which runs world soccer, and UEFA, which runs European soccer. But Poland says it won't stop the Under-20 Women's World Cup from kicking off next month. Here's the backstory: UEFA's 55 member countries voted to boycott—or refuse to join—FIFA events. They're mad at FIFA's president, Gianni Infantino, because he wanted to sell part of the World Cup's money-making rights to private investors for about $4.2 billion. He later dropped the plan, but UEFA still doesn't trust him. Despite the drama, Poland, the host country, says everything is on schedule. "Preparations are in their final stage," the Polish soccer federation said. They haven't heard of any team pulling out. France and New Zealand have already confirmed they'll send teams. A New Zealand spokesperson said the tournament is "critical" for developing women's soccer. The tournament runs from September 5 to 27 with 24 teams. The US is expected to play too, but they haven't said anything officially yet. England and Canada are staying quiet for now. UEFA doubled down last week, saying they've "lost confidence" in Infantino. But for now, the games will go on. If the fight gets worse, other women's tournaments later this year could be in trouble. But for the young players heading to Poland, this is their chance to shine on a world stage—and no grown-up argument is going to take that away.
why_it_matters: Even when big organizations argue, young athletes get a chance to show their skills on a world stage, and you can see how sports can bring people together despite conflict.

background_read: FIFA (the world's soccer organization) and UEFA (the European soccer group) usually work together to run tournaments.
Gianni Infantino is the president of FIFA. Women's soccer has been growing quickly, and the Under-20 World Cup is a big event for young players hoping to become stars.
Poland (a country in Europe) is excited to host the tournament for the first time.
Article_Structure: WHO: FIFA, UEFA, Gianni Infantino, Poland as host, and the 24 women's teams, including France and New Zealand
WHAT: UEFA is boycotting FIFA events, but Poland insists the Under-20 Women's World Cup will still happen on schedule
WHERE: In Poland, where the tournament will take place in September
WHY: Because UEFA lost trust in FIFA's president over a money plan, but the host country and teams want the tournament to go on for the players' sake

perspectives.description: They are angry at FIFA's president because they think he made a secret plan to sell World Cup rights and they no longer trust him.
They have worked hard to prepare for the tournament and say everything is ready, no matter the fight between the big soccer bosses.
For young players from France, New Zealand, and other countries, this tournament is a dream chance to play against the best and get noticed by fans and coaches.
